context:
Cause (found in Theseus, joeharris76/theseus): the #3950 D1 reviews were forced dispute re-reviews (protocol marker forced=true, same patch digest). In forced rounds protocol.judge(rejudge_fixed=True) and report.effective_status rewrite a reviewer's `fixed` disposition to not_fixed, and report.disposition_label maps not_fixed to "maintained", while the published rationale (the reviewer's evidence) still said the fallback fixes it. The prompt (render.DISPUTE_RULE) offered `fixed` for disputes, so the model chose it; the old test test_a_forced_fixed_counts_as_maintained_in_the_published_line pinned the contradiction. Each such round counted toward escalation, so after 2 rounds the gate escalated to the owner.
Fix: joeharris76/theseus PR #41, merged as d160e4483738da2885ea94e931b3e2bd4ced836c (on top of 0.2.4). A `fixed` disposition on a disputed finding in a forced round is now an invalid verdict (protocol.forced_fixed_problems, checked in protocol.contradiction regardless of the decision), so it is retried with a message steering to withdrawn+concedes or not_fixed; the prompt now requires status to agree with the evidence and says never to mark fixed on an unchanged patch. Regression tests in tests/unit/reviewer/test_dispute_keyed_evidence.py (forced fixed invalid for shipping and non-shipping decisions; withdrawn, not_fixed and unforced fixed unaffected); dispute_round golden regenerated; docs/local-review.md updated. Theseus full suite 3917 passed, CI green.
Next step: re-pin BenchBox to the Theseus commit at or after d160e4483738da2885ea94e931b3e2bd4ced836c (lock + caller pin, per the Theseus re-lock procedure), then finish this item. Not re-pinned here by instruction. The gate exit-3 noise was fixed separately in Theseus PR #40 (9d37867), released in 0.2.4 (PR #42); it rides the same re-pin.

Acceptance gap, recorded deliberately: the #3950 dispute was not replayed, because only the comment's protocol marker is public and the reviewer's disposition JSON is not. Theseus #41 instead adds regression tests for the forced-round path: a forced `fixed` disposition is rejected and retried, while withdrawn, not_fixed and unforced fixed are unaffected. The contradictory label is no longer reachable on an unchanged patch. Closed by owner instruction on 2026-11-09, with the replay gap noted.
description:
Problem. On PR #3950 head ec6e41c1416fe2ffd648eb3293c67cd3871b6f4d, finding D1 (High: DuckDB Vortex routing loads 0 rows) was fixed and disputed twice with file:line evidence. Both oracle-verdict reviews (2026-11-06 04:19 and 04:30 UTC) marked the dispute 'D1 (maintained)', yet the disposition text explained why the fallback catches the failure and cited the covering test. The gate escalated to the owner, who withdrew D1 by adjudication. The verdict and its rationale contradicted each other, and this cost an owner action and about an hour.

Change. Find where the dispute disposition label (maintained or withdrawn) is decided relative to the reviewer's text, and make them consistent: the label is derived from or checked against the rationale, or a mismatch is flagged rather than escalated. Related: oracle-flags-code-outside-the-diff-and-dispute-does-not-rerun-20261101 and oracle-dispute-and-rerun-live-observation-20261030.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone; no explanatory comments (make comment-policy-check); changelog.d fragment if user-facing; re-read cited symbols before editing; never bypass a required check or relax a ruleset (owner-only).
